commits: 25933c3 scripts: repair after verification round 4 (entry tooling, issues 1 to 11)
9bbd5bf evidence/lean: records of a full run of scripts/check.sh --fresh on 25933c3
key_sentences: A default full run of the checks (`sh scripts/check.sh --fresh` on commit `25933c3` of branch `fix/tooling2`; its records in `evidence/lean/` are commit `9bbd5bf`) passed.

It establishes that `lakefile.toml`, `lake-manifest.json` and `lean-toolchain` are the pinned files. `lakefile.toml` has no key outside the short list that step 2 accepts, so no key such as `srcDir`, `roots` or `moreLeanArgs` can move the library's sources or build products or pass arguments to the compiler. Each of the nine dependency checkouts in `.lake/packages` is at the revision given in `lake-manifest.json`, and `git status` lists no changed and no untracked file in it.

All 23 modules of the library were compiled in that run from the 37 files (build configuration, library sources, design file, checking scripts) whose digests are recorded in `evidence/lean/sources.sha256`, taken before the first step and again at the end. No module of a dependency was compiled.

The design record `VoltageToBit/Examples/IllustrativeDesign.lean`, named in `scripts/design-records.txt`, is byte for byte what `scripts/gen_design.py` generates from `designs/illustrative-1v8.json`, and no other `.lean` file of the library carries the generator's header.

The source scan (Lean's own parser against the allow-list) and the axiom audit found nothing. None of the 556 declarations stored in the compiled files of the library, 329 of which are written in the source files, depends on an axiom other than `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

Lean's kernel (`leanchecker`) re-checked the 553 declarations of the compiled files of the 23 modules, each module on top of its imports as compiled. The other 3 stored declarations are compiler auxiliaries that the replay leaves out.

An export of these 553 declarations, with the 44,448 declarations of Mathlib, its dependencies and Lean core that they depend on, was accepted by the six checkers bundled with the toolchain. `leanchecker` starts from an empty environment, as its source shows. `leanchecker-paranoid`, `lean4lean` and `nanoda` each refuse an export without the declaration of `Eq` (observed; their sources were not read). `con-leche` and `con-ron` start from a prelude built into them.
The self-test of the scripts (`sh scripts/selftest.sh`, output in `evidence/selftest/selftest-9bbd5bf.txt`) passed on commit `9bbd5bf` with 85 PASS lines and no FAIL line.

Of the 85 PASS lines, 71 are negative controls: a defect that `check.sh` must report at the step that is meant to catch it, or an attack that must change nothing. They include the attacks of verification round 4 on the file tree, on Python's search path, on `lakefile.toml`, on the design record and on `.lake/config`. 7 are positive controls (an unmodified input that must pass), 6 are observations of what the six export checkers start from, and 1 is the check that the checkout was not changed.

A pass does not establish that the statements mean what the prose says or that any physical device obeys the model. It establishes nothing when the library itself is hostile: library code can run while it is compiled, before any check runs.

Nor does it establish that the export is faithful, that the four checkers other than Lean's kernel are sound or independent of each other, or anything about declarations of Mathlib that the library does not depend on. `--whole-env` would re-check those of the imported modules, but it was not run for this commit.

Further limits: the audit's shadowing rule does not consider names that `open` makes visible; a definition of type `Design` that `scripts/design-records.txt` does not name is compared with no JSON file; files that a dependency's `.gitignore` excludes are not looked at; and `--quick` reads the record of the last full run as it is.

Two checks of `check.sh` have no control in the self-test: the `git status` check of the dependency checkouts, and the comparison, in a full run, of the modules Lake reported as built with the audited ones.

Requirements: the toolchain named in `lean-toolchain` (through elan); Mathlib and its dependencies checked out in `.lake/packages` at the revisions in `lake-manifest.json`, with nothing changed, and compiled (`lake build` fetches and compiles them once); and `python3` 3.11 or later and `git`, both found through `PATH`.

`scripts/check.sh` and `scripts/selftest.sh` run every Python program with `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` and `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1`, so no module is imported from the project directory. Both stop with exit status 2 if `python3` is older than 3.11, and `check.sh` also does if `git` is not found. `check.sh` downloads nothing.

Measured with `/usr/bin/time -l` on an Apple M3 Pro laptop (12 cores, 18 GB of memory, macOS 14.4), while Lean jobs of other sessions were running (load average between about 2.4 and 4.2), with `CHECK_REPLAY_JOBS=1` and the other settings at their defaults: `sh scripts/check.sh --fresh` took 634 s (about 11 min), with at most 3.1 GB resident in one process; `sh scripts/selftest.sh` took 3609 s (about 60 min), with at most 4.2 GB resident in one process.
This repair (branch `fix/tooling2`, commits `25933c3`, `9bbd5bf` and `4c20531`) has not yet been verified by an independent reviewer.

issues.description: Step 2's new check runs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=normal` in each checkout, with the checkout's own git configuration and the user's (HOME is passed on). Git does not report a changed tracked file whose index entry is marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree. It does not report an untracked file that .git/info/exclude or the user's global excludes file matches. With core.worktree set in the checkout's .git/config, it looks at another directory. Step 2 then accepts a changed checkout, so 'with nothing changed' says more than it checks, and the parenthetical names .gitignore only.

confirmed_sentences: A default full run of the checks (`sh scripts/check.sh --fresh` on commit `25933c3` of branch `fix/tooling2`; its records in `evidence/lean/` are commit `9bbd5bf`) passed.

It establishes that `lakefile.toml`, `lake-manifest.json` and `lean-toolchain` are the pinned files. `lakefile.toml` has no key outside the short list that step 2 accepts, so no key such as `srcDir`, `roots` or `moreLeanArgs` can move the library's sources or build products or pass extra arguments to the compiler. The options under `[leanOptions]`, one of the accepted keys, do reach the compiler, and only the pin fixes them. Each of the nine dependency checkouts in `.lake/packages` is at the revision given in `lake-manifest.json`, and `git status` lists no changed and no untracked file in it.

All 23 modules of the library were compiled in that run from its source files. The digests of the 37 checked files (build configuration, library sources, design file, checking scripts) are recorded in `evidence/lean/sources.sha256`; they were taken before the first step and again at the end, and agreed. No module of a dependency was compiled.

The design record `VoltageToBit/Examples/IllustrativeDesign.lean`, named in `scripts/design-records.txt`, is byte for byte what `scripts/gen_design.py` generates from `designs/illustrative-1v8.json` under the definition name `illustrative`, and no other `.lean` file of the library begins with the generator's header.

The source scan (Lean's own parser against the allow-list) and the axiom audit found nothing. None of the 556 declarations stored in the compiled files of the library, 329 of which are written in the source files, depends on an axiom other than `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.

Lean's kernel (`leanchecker`) re-checked the 553 declarations of the compiled files of the 23 modules, each module on top of its imports as compiled. The other 3 stored declarations are compiler auxiliaries that the replay leaves out.

An export of these 553 declarations, with the 44,448 declarations of Mathlib, its dependencies and Lean core that they depend on, was accepted by the six checkers bundled with the toolchain. `leanchecker` starts from an empty environment, as its source shows. `leanchecker-paranoid`, `lean4lean` and `nanoda` each refuse an export without the declaration of `Eq` (observed; their sources were not read). `con-leche` and `con-ron` start from a prelude built into them.
The self-test of the scripts (`sh scripts/selftest.sh`, output in `evidence/selftest/selftest-9bbd5bf.txt`) passed on commit `9bbd5bf` with 85 PASS lines and no FAIL line.

Of the 85 PASS lines, 71 are negative controls: a defect that `check.sh` must report at the step that is meant to catch it, or an attack that must change nothing. In 4 of them the program of that step (the scan, the design generator or the audit) is run directly. They include the attacks of verification round 4 on the file tree, on Python's search path, on `lakefile.toml`, on the design record and on `.lake/config`. 7 are positive controls (an unmodified input that must pass), 6 are observations of what the six export checkers start from, and 1 is the check that the checkout was not changed.

A pass does not establish that the statements mean what the prose says or that any physical device obeys the model. It establishes nothing when the library itself is hostile: library code can run while it is compiled, before any check runs.

Nor does it establish that the export is faithful, that the four checkers other than Lean's kernel are sound or independent of each other, or anything about declarations of Mathlib that the library does not depend on. `--whole-env` would re-check those of the imported modules, but it was not run for this commit.

Requirements: the toolchain named in `lean-toolchain` (through elan); Mathlib and its dependencies checked out in `.lake/packages` at the revisions in `lake-manifest.json`, with nothing changed, and compiled (`lake build` fetches and compiles them once); and `python3` 3.11 or later and `git`, both found through `PATH`.

`scripts/check.sh` and `scripts/selftest.sh` run every Python program with `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1` and `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1`, so no module is imported from the project directory. Both stop with exit status 2 if `python3` is older than 3.11, and `check.sh` also does if `git` is not found. `check.sh` downloads nothing.

Measured with `/usr/bin/time -l` on an Apple M3 Pro laptop (12 cores, 18 GB of memory, macOS 14.4), while Lean jobs of other sessions were running (load average between about 2.4 and 4.2), with `CHECK_REPLAY_JOBS=1` and the other settings at their defaults: `sh scripts/check.sh --fresh` took 634 s (about 11 min), with at most 3.1 GB resident in one process; `sh scripts/selftest.sh` took 3609 s (about 60 min), with at most 4.2 GB resident in one process.

An independent verifier checked this repair (branch `fix/tooling2`, commits `25933c3`, `9bbd5bf` and `4c20531`) after verification round 4. Every attack of verification rounds 2 and 4 now stops at the step meant to catch it or changes nothing. A fresh copy of the branch in another directory reproduced the five records of `evidence/lean/` byte for byte, and its `scripts/selftest.sh` printed the committed output line for line. The verifier did not pass the repair, for two reasons. With the pin changed, `[leanOptions]` can carry an option that changes what a statement means (`deprecated.oldSectionVars`), and a full run then passes. And the `git status` check of step 2 does not see every change to a dependency checkout.
